b:
When I wondered what to write about, it was Na. Muthukumar's essays that pushed me to write about myself. For someone used to enjoying only poems, the colour of poetry in an essay tasted like mountain honey turned to wine

Following him, I too

Rathi Mami

The one who teaches you letters is God

My father's family was well known in the village as "the teachers' compound". From my great-grandfather down, it was a family vowed to give one teacher to every generation. My mother's side was no less; through her grandfather it was a line of teachers too. So numbers and letters must have soaked into my very flesh

That must be what my mother thought too. The one who started me on my letters was my aunt's grandfather, a learned man. I wrote with my hand in his. I could have ended up a blot that never saw the lighthouse

The letters did not come to me

My time went by in cartoons

Back then, the one who belled the cat was Rathi Mami

From our house it was five minutes to hers. You had to go past her house. A big house.. a big compound. On the white door the brass numbers 33 would gleam. In the back compound there was a well and a kennel.. Since I wasn't allowed to play with the dog, my border ended at the kennel door.. Inside there was a bunker room.. Uncle would be there.. I wasn't allowed to disturb him

Whenever we went from our house to the shops, we had to pass that house.. On the way it was a stop for Amma. A halt.. Since she carried me, she must have needed a place to put me down… if anyone had told me, I'd have tried to walk the day I was born.. Fate.. I would be imprisoned in that house every day..

It was a reformatory.. No child at the nearby school studied without passing through Mami's hands.. There are stories of those who escaped too… I am one who tried to be one of them and failed

She told my dough-soft hands to hold a pencil.. She banned cartoons and told me to read storybooks… I bit and tore at things. At once she would grip my hands tight and put them in my own mouth..

She was the Yashoda who tied me to a chair like the little one whose mouth held the world…

Say what you like, the world she opened for me that day was a rare one.. From that day I lost myself entirely in the world of books.… Reading and buying books wherever I went became a habit, and the bookworm of those days now flutters about like a butterfly..

Later, when we moved house, what made me happiest was thinking I would no longer have to be imprisoned with Rathi Mami.. But it was she who sought me out even there and led me into English books

Later we lost touch.. After a long time, grown up, I went to her house.

The house that stood so vast in my memory, and its compound, looked small then.. But Mami alone was there, just the same… At once, from somewhere, the little one whose mouth held the world came running out inside me…

Dedicated to her, and to the books that, because of her, have piled up and keep piling up in my house to this day
note: Na. Muthukumar was a celebrated Tamil lyricist and essayist. Bala Kandam, "the book of childhood", is the first book of the Ramayana. Mami is an aunt. Yashoda once tied the child Krishna to a mortar for his mischief; Krishna is also the child who showed the whole universe inside his mouth.
